doc.title: Virginia Mayhew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2022

chapter: Working with Al Grey and Diva
title: Al Grey and his tune 'Echoes of New Orleans'
summary: Rowe recalls Al Grey's hit-hopeful tune; Mayhew says she wrote out and arranged his simple tunes and he was fully energized on stage.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let’s talk about Al Grey for a minute. He was one of the first people we interviewed way back in ’95, and then a couple of years later I happened to go to Sweet Basil’s and he was playing there. And he played this tune called “Echoes of New Orleans.” It was so catchy. And afterwards I went up to him and I said, “Mr. Grey, that is the coolest tune.” And he goes, “Yeah, I got a hit!” And I thought that’s so cool that this guy, that he was probably in his late 70s at least, and that he had a hit.
Was it actually a hit or did he think it was a hit?
He thought it was a hit.
Or it was going to be.
Yeah. He was so enthusiastic. What? I’m sorry.
I said it should have been a hit because it was an earworm.
Um hum. I’ve got to write that down, what was it called?

Yeah. He composed a lot of tunes, like simple little tunes, and when I was working with him I would written them down and then write little arrangements for them. And he was always coming up with new things. [to off camera *** 44:22] can you just finish, and go? Thanks. It’s so distracting.
That’s okay, we can edit that.
And I keep losing my train of thought.
We were talking about Al and his tunes.
Oh Al. Yep. And he would — once he got on stage he was a hundred percent, a hundred percent. And it was a great experience working with him.
